name: Keo Siu Chau
summary: A peanut and sesame candy cooked with sugar and malt, rolled thin, and cut into bite-size pieces. Dân trí says it has more peanut and less malt than ordinary kẹo lạc, so it is crisp, fragrant, and does not stick to the teeth.
origin: Nam Định. The Nam Định city portal on 17 October 2018 and Dân Việt on 5 September 2025 name it as a gift. VnExpress, 18 March 2016, and Dân trí, 4 March 2017, describe it. Báo Nam Định lists it as an OCOP product and a city gift.
texture: Dân trí: crisp, nutty, lightly sweet, not sticky on the teeth. VnExpress: the hot mass is poured onto a tray dusted with sticky-rice flour, rolled thin, and cut into bite-size pieces.
howToEat: As a piece to carry. Dân trí and Thế giới tiếp thị say it is especially eaten at Tết, with a cup of hot tea.
where: The city. VnExpress ties the name to an old candy shop at bến sông Vị Hoàng.
seoTitle: Keo Siu Chau — peanut candy from Nam Dinh
seoDescription: Peanut and sesame candy, crisper and less malty than ordinary kẹo lạc on Dân trí’s account. Eat it with hot tea.
